text:
Flowering (stage R1, silking) typically occurs around 50-60 days after emergence, though this varies by variety and conditions (see the variety table for specific days-to-flowering ranges). Silks emerge from the tip of the ear at roughly the same time the tassel is shedding pollen, and this timing overlap (synchrony) is essential for good pollination -- see the pollination biology topic for more detail.

This flowering window, together with the couple of weeks around it, is widely regarded as the single most sensitive period in the corn crop's life to drought, heat, or nutrient stress. Stress during this window can cause poor kernel set (gaps or blank sections on the cob) even in an otherwise healthy-looking crop, so maintaining good soil moisture and nutrition through this period is a high management priority.
